revision.text:
{{Short description|Archaeological site in Myōkō, Hokuriku, Japan}} {{Use American English|date=April 2021}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | name = Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun group | native_name = 観音平・天神堂古墳群 | native_name_lang = | image =Kan-nondaira Kofun Group, gaikan.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Kofun in the Kannondaira Kofun group | map_type = Japan Niigata Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun group | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|37|03|36|N|138|13|55|E|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Myōkō, Niigata]], [[Japan]] | region = [[Hokuriku region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = 101,160 sq meters | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = | abandoned = | epochs = [[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes | other_designation = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = | notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} }} The {{nihongo|'''Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster'''|観音平・天神堂古墳群|Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun-gun}} is an [[archaeological site]] containing two separate groups of early to middle[[Kofun period]] [[kofun|burial tumulii]] located in what is now part of the city of [[Myōkō, Niigata]] in the [[Hokuriku region]] of [[Japan]]. The site was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1978.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/201486 |title=観音平・天神堂古墳群|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 30, 2020}}</ref>
==Overview== The Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster consists of two separate groups of ''kofun'', approximately {{Convert|1|km|4=1|sp=us|spell=in}} apart, located approximately 10 minutes by car from [[Arai Station (Niigata)|Arai Station]] on the [[JR East]] [[Shinetsu Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The '''Kannondaira Site''' contains three groups of approximately 53 tumuli, including one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tomb]] ({{nihongo|''zenpō-kōen-fun''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}) dating from the 3rd century. Most of the tombs are {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=dome-shaped|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ({{nihongo|''empun''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), although one is {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=scallop-shaped|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} ({{nihongo|''hotategai-gata kofun''|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}) and some are {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-shaped|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} ({{nihongo|''hōfun''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}), indicating that the site is from a transitional period between the [[Yayoi period]] and the Kofun period. ''[[Haniwa]]'' and ''[[fukiishi]]'' have been recovered from the area. The keyhole-shaped tomb is designated No.4 in the group, and has a total length of {{Convert|33.6|m|sp=us}}, with a dome-portion measuring {{Convert|19.0|by|23.0|m|sp=us}}, and a trapezoidal portion with length of {{Convert|11.6|m|sp=us}} and width of {{Convert|7.0|m|sp=us}}, narrowing to {{Convert|5.0|m|sp=us}} at the "neck" where it connects with the dome. No [[grave goods]] were found in this tomb.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The '''Tenjindō Site''' also consists of three groups of tumuli, of which 188 have thus far been catalogued, making it one of the largest sites in Niigata Prefecture. Almost all of the tumuli are small and dome-shaped, with diameters between {{Convert|5|and|25|m|sp=us|spell=in}}. The site has been repeatedly [[archaeological excavation|excavated]] by [[Tokyo University]]. [[Grave goods]] recovered include [[Sue pottery]], [[Shinju-kyo|bronze mirrors]], straight iron swords, parts of armor, horse fittings and items of jewellery. From these grave goods, it is estimated that these tumuli were constructed from the late 5th century to the late 6th century.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The two sites flank a large moated late [[Yayoi period]] to early Kofun-period settlement, the [[Hida Sites|Hida Site]], which has a separate National Historic Site designation. The Kannondaira cluster is to the north, and the Tenjindō cluster is to the south, and these areas may have been the necropolis for this settlement. As the area was mostly covered in forest, the state of preservation was relatively good, although even in 1976 it had been reported that a number of the known ''kofun'' has been destroyed due to urban encroachment, road construction, landslides and robbery. After the designation as a National Historic Site, the area has been cleared and opened to the public as an [[archaeological park]], with a small museum to display some of the artifacts found.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

{{Short description|Archaeological site in Myōkō, Hokuriku, Japan}} {{Use American English|date=April 2021}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | name = Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun group | native_name = 観音平・天神堂古墳群 | native_name_lang = | image =Kan-nondaira Kofun Group, gaikan.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Kofun in the Kannondaira Kofun group | map_type = Japan Niigata Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun group | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|37|03|36|N|138|13|55|E|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Myōkō, Niigata]], [[Japan]] | region = [[Hokuriku region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = 101,160 sq meters | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = | abandoned = | epochs = [[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes | other_designation = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = | notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} }} The {{nihongo|'''Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster'''|観音平・天神堂古墳群|Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun-gun}} is an [[archaeological site]] containing two separate groups of early to middle[[Kofun period]] [[kofun|burial tumulii]] located in what is now part of the city of [[Myōkō, Niigata]] in the [[Hokuriku region]] of [[Japan]]. The site was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1978.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/201486 |title=観音平・天神堂古墳群|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 30, 2020}}</ref>
==Overview== The Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster consists of two separate groups of ''kofun'', approximately {{Convert|1|km|4=1|sp=us|spell=in}} apart, located approximately 10 minutes by car from [[Arai Station (Niigata)|Arai Station]] on the [[JR East]] [[Shinetsu Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The '''Kannondaira Site''' contains three groups of approximately 53 tumuli, including one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tomb]] ({{nihongo|''zenpō-kōen-fun''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}) dating from the 3rd century. Most of the tombs are {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=dome-shaped|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ({{nihongo|''empun''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), although one is {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=scallop-shaped|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} ({{nihongo|''hotategai-gata kofun''|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}) and some are {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-shaped|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} ({{nihongo|''hōfun''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}), indicating that the site is from a transitional period between the [[Yayoi period]] and the Kofun period. ''[[Haniwa]]'' and ''[[fukiishi]]'' have been recovered from the area. The keyhole-shaped tomb is designated No.4 in the group, and has a total length of {{Convert|33.6|m|sp=us}}, with a dome-portion measuring {{Convert|19.0|by|23.0|m|sp=us}}, and a trapezoidal portion with length of {{Convert|11.6|m|sp=us}} and width of {{Convert|7.0|m|sp=us}}, narrowing to {{Convert|5.0|m|sp=us}} at the "neck" where it connects with the dome. No [[grave goods]] were found in this tomb.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The '''Tenjindō Site''' also consists of three groups of tumuli, of which 188 have thus far been catalogued, making it one of the largest sites in Niigata Prefecture. Almost all of the tumuli are small and dome-shaped, with diameters between {{Convert|5|and|25|m|sp=us|spell=in}}. The site has been repeatedly [[archaeological excavation|excavated]] by [[Tokyo University]]. [[Grave goods]] recovered include [[Sue pottery]], [[Shinju-kyo|bronze mirrors]], straight iron swords, parts of armor, horse fittings and items of jewellery. From these grave goods, it is estimated that these tumuli were constructed from the late 5th century to the late 6th century.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The two sites flank a large moated late [[Yayoi period]] to early Kofun-period settlement, the [[Hida Sites|Hida Site]], which has a separate National Historic Site designation. The Kannondaira cluster is to the north, and the Tenjindō cluster is to the south, and these areas may have been the necropolis for this settlement. As the area was mostly covered in forest, the state of preservation was relatively good, although even in 1976 it had been reported that a number of the known ''kofun'' has been destroyed due to urban encroachment, road construction, landslides and robbery. After the designation as a National Historic Site, the area has been cleared and opened to the public as an [[archaeological park]], with a small museum to display some of the artifacts found.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

{{Short description|Archaeological site in Myōkō, Hokuriku, Japan}} {{Use American English|date=April 2021}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | name = Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun group | native_name = 観音平・天神堂古墳群 | native_name_lang = | image =Kan-nondaira Kofun Group, gaikan.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Kofun in the Kannondaira Kofun group | map_type = Japan Niigata Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun group | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|37|03|36|N|138|13|55|E|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Myōkō, Niigata]], [[Japan]] | region = [[Hokuriku region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = 101,160 sq meters | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = | abandoned = | epochs = [[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes | Historic Site = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = | notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} }} The {{nihongo|'''Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster'''|観音平・天神堂古墳群|Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun-gun}} is an [[archaeological site]] containing two separate groups of early to middle[[Kofun period]] [[kofun|burial tumulii]] located in what is now part of the city of [[Myōkō, Niigata]] in the [[Hokuriku region]] of [[Japan]]. The site was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1978.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/201486 |title=観音平・天神堂古墳群|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 30, 2020}}</ref>
==Overview== The Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster consists of two separate groups of ''kofun'', approximately {{Convert|1|km|4=1|sp=us|spell=in}} apart, located approximately 10 minutes by car from [[Arai Station (Niigata)|Arai Station]] on the [[JR East]] [[Shinetsu Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The '''Kannondaira Site''' contains three groups of approximately 53 tumuli, including one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tomb]] ({{nihongo|''zenpō-kōen-fun''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}) dating from the 3rd century. Most of the tombs are {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=dome-shaped|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ({{nihongo|''empun''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), although one is {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=scallop-shaped|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} ({{nihongo|''hotategai-gata kofun''|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}) and some are {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-shaped|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} ({{nihongo|''hōfun''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}), indicating that the site is from a transitional period between the [[Yayoi period]] and the Kofun period. ''[[Haniwa]]'' and ''[[fukiishi]]'' have been recovered from the area. The keyhole-shaped tomb is designated No.4 in the group, and has a total length of {{Convert|33.6|m|sp=us}}, with a dome-portion measuring {{Convert|19.0|by|23.0|m|sp=us}}, and a trapezoidal portion with length of {{Convert|11.6|m|sp=us}} and width of {{Convert|7.0|m|sp=us}}, narrowing to {{Convert|5.0|m|sp=us}} at the "neck" where it connects with the dome. No [[grave goods]] were found in this tomb.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The '''Tenjindō Site''' also consists of three groups of tumuli, of which 188 have thus far been catalogued, making it one of the largest sites in Niigata Prefecture. Almost all of the tumuli are small and dome-shaped, with diameters between {{Convert|5|and|25|m|sp=us|spell=in}}. The site has been repeatedly [[archaeological excavation|excavated]] by [[Tokyo University]]. [[Grave goods]] recovered include [[Sue pottery]], [[Shinju-kyo|bronze mirrors]], straight iron swords, parts of armor, horse fittings and items of jewellery. From these grave goods, it is estimated that these tumuli were constructed from the late 5th century to the late 6th century.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The two sites flank a large moated late [[Yayoi period]] to early Kofun-period settlement, the [[Hida Sites|Hida Site]], which has a separate National Historic Site designation. The Kannondaira cluster is to the north, and the Tenjindō cluster is to the south, and these areas may have been the necropolis for this settlement. As the area was mostly covered in forest, the state of preservation was relatively good, although even in 1976 it had been reported that a number of the known ''kofun'' has been destroyed due to urban encroachment, road construction, landslides and robbery. After the designation as a National Historic Site, the area has been cleared and opened to the public as an [[archaeological park]], with a small museum to display some of the artifacts found.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

{{Short description|Archaeological site in Myōkō, Hokuriku, Japan}} {{Use American English|date=April 2021}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | name = Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun group | native_name = 観音平・天神堂古墳群 | native_name_lang = | image =Kan-nondaira Kofun Group, gaikan.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Kofun in the Kannondaira Kofun group | map_type = Japan Niigata Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun group | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|37|03|36|N|138|13|55|E|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Myōkō, Niigata]], [[Japan]] | region = [[Hokuriku region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = 101,160 sq meters | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = | abandoned = | epochs = [[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes | Historic Site = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = | notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} }} The {{nihongo|'''Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster'''|観音平・天神堂古墳群|Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun-gun}} is an [[archaeological site]] containing two separate groups of early to middle[[Kofun period]] [[kofun|burial tumulii]] located in what is now part of the city of [[Myōkō, Niigata]] in the [[Hokuriku region]] of [[Japan]]. The site was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1978.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/201486 |title=観音平・天神堂古墳群|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 30, 2020}}</ref>
==Overview== The Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster consists of two separate groups of ''kofun'', approximately {{Convert|1|km|4=1|sp=us|spell=in}} apart, located approximately 10 minutes by car from [[Arai Station (Niigata)|Arai Station]] on the [[JR East]] [[Shinetsu Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The '''Kannondaira Site''' contains three groups of approximately 53 tumuli, including one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tomb]] ({{nihongo|''zenpō-kōen-fun''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}) dating from the 3rd century. Most of the tombs are {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=dome-shaped|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ({{nihongo|''empun''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), although one is {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=scallop-shaped|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} ({{nihongo|''hotategai-gata kofun''|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}) and some are {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-shaped|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} ({{nihongo|''hōfun''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}), indicating that the site is from a transitional period between the [[Yayoi period]] and the Kofun period. ''[[Haniwa]]'' and ''[[fukiishi]]'' have been recovered from the area. The keyhole-shaped tomb is designated No.4 in the group, and has a total length of {{Convert|33.6|m|sp=us}}, with a dome-portion measuring {{Convert|19.0|by|23.0|m|sp=us}}, and a trapezoidal portion with length of {{Convert|11.6|m|sp=us}} and width of {{Convert|7.0|m|sp=us}}, narrowing to {{Convert|5.0|m|sp=us}} at the "neck" where it connects with the dome. No [[grave goods]] were found in this tomb.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The '''Tenjindō Site''' also consists of three groups of tumuli, of which 188 have thus far been catalogued, making it one of the largest sites in Niigata Prefecture. Almost all of the tumuli are small and dome-shaped, with diameters between {{Convert|5|and|25|m|sp=us|spell=in}}. The site has been repeatedly [[archaeological excavation|excavated]] by [[Tokyo University]]. [[Grave goods]] recovered include [[Sue pottery]], [[Shinju-kyo|bronze mirrors]], straight iron swords, parts of armor, horse fittings and items of jewellery. From these grave goods, it is estimated that these tumuli were constructed from the late 5th century to the late 6th century.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The two sites flank a large moated late [[Yayoi period]] to early Kofun-period settlement, the [[Hida Sites|Hida Site]], which has a separate National Historic Site designation. The Kannondaira cluster is to the north, and the Tenjindō cluster is to the south, and these areas may have been the necropolis for this settlement. As the area was mostly covered in forest, the state of preservation was relatively good, although even in 1976 it had been reported that a number of the known ''kofun'' has been destroyed due to urban encroachment, road construction, landslides and robbery. After the designation as a National Historic Site, the area has been cleared and opened to the public as an [[archaeological park]], with a small museum to display some of the artifacts found.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

{{Short description|Archaeological site in Myōkō, Hokuriku, Japan}} {{Use American English|date=April 2021}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | name = Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun group | native_name = 観音平・天神堂古墳群 | native_name_lang = | image =Kan-nondaira Kofun Group, gaikan.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Kofun in the Kannondaira Kofun group | map_type = Japan Niigata Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun group | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|37|03|36|N|138|13|55|E|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Myōkō, Niigata]], [[Japan]] | region = [[Hokuriku region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = 101,160 sq meters | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = | abandoned = | epochs = [[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes | Historic Site = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = | notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} }} The {{nihongo|'''Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster'''|観音平・天神堂古墳群|Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun-gun}} is an [[archaeological site]] containing two separate groups of early to middle[[Kofun period]] [[kofun|burial tumulii]] located in what is now part of the city of [[Myōkō, Niigata]] in the [[Hokuriku region]] of [[Japan]]. The site was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1978.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/201486 |title=観音平・天神堂古墳群|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 30, 2020}}</ref>
==Overview== The Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster consists of two separate groups of ''kofun'', approximately {{Convert|1|km|4=1|sp=us|spell=in}} apart, located approximately 10 minutes by car from [[Arai Station (Niigata)|Arai Station]] on the [[JR East]] [[Shinetsu Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The '''Kannondaira Site''' contains three groups of approximately 53 tumuli, including one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tomb]] ({{nihongo|''zenpō-kōen-fun''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}) dating from the 3rd century. Most of the tombs are {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=dome-shaped|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ({{nihongo|''empun''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), although one is {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=scallop-shaped|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} ({{nihongo|''hotategai-gata kofun''|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}) and some are {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-shaped|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} ({{nihongo|''hōfun''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}), indicating that the site is from a transitional period between the [[Yayoi period]] and the Kofun period. ''[[Haniwa]]'' and ''[[fukiishi]]'' have been recovered from the area. The keyhole-shaped tomb is designated No.4 in the group, and has a total length of {{Convert|33.6|m|sp=us}}, with a dome-portion measuring {{Convert|19.0|by|23.0|m|sp=us}}, and a trapezoidal portion with length of {{Convert|11.6|m|sp=us}} and width of {{Convert|7.0|m|sp=us}}, narrowing to {{Convert|5.0|m|sp=us}} at the "neck" where it connects with the dome. No [[grave goods]] were found in this tomb.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The '''Tenjindō Site''' also consists of three groups of tumuli, of which 188 have thus far been catalogued, making it one of the largest sites in Niigata Prefecture. Almost all of the tumuli are small and dome-shaped, with diameters between {{Convert|5|and|25|m|sp=us|spell=in}}. The site has been repeatedly [[archaeological excavation|excavated]] by [[Tokyo University]]. [[Grave goods]] recovered include [[Sue pottery]], [[Shinju-kyo|bronze mirrors]], straight iron swords, parts of armor, horse fittings and items of jewellery. From these grave goods, it is estimated that these tumuli were constructed from the late 5th century to the late 6th century.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The two sites flank a large moated late [[Yayoi period]] to early Kofun-period settlement, the [[Hida Sites|Hida Site]], which has a separate National Historic Site designation. The Kannondaira cluster is to the north, and the Tenjindō cluster is to the south, and these areas may have been the necropolis for this settlement. As the area was mostly covered in forest, the state of preservation was relatively good, although even in 1976 it had been reported that a number of the known ''kofun'' has been destroyed due to urban encroachment, road construction, landslides and robbery. After the designation as a National Historic Site, the area has been cleared and opened to the public as an [[archaeological park]], with a small museum to display some of the artifacts found.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
==See also== *[[List of Historic Sites of Japan (Niigata)]]

Most of the tombs are {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=dome-shaped|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ({{nihongo|''empun''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), although one is {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=scallop-shaped|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{nihongo|''hotategai-gata kofun''|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}) and some are {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-shaped|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{nihongo|''hōfun''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}), indicating that the site is from a transitional period between the [[Yayoi period]] and the Kofun period. ''[[Haniwa]]'' and ''[[fukiishi]]'' have been recovered from the area. The keyhole-shaped tomb is designated No.4 in the group, and has a total length of {{Convert|33.6|m|sp=us}}, with a dome-portion measuring {{Convert|19.0|by|23.0|m|sp=us}}, and a trapezoidal portion with length of {{Convert|11.6|m|sp=us}} and width of {{Convert|7.0|m|sp=us}}, narrowing to {{Convert|5.0|m|sp=us}} at the "neck" where it connects with the dome. No [[grave goods]] were found in this tomb.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The '''Tenjindō Site''' also consists of three groups of tumuli, of which 188 have thus far been catalogued, making it one of the largest sites in Niigata Prefecture. Almost all of the tumuli are small and dome-shaped, with diameters between {{Convert|5|and|25|m|sp=us|spell=in}}. The site has been repeatedly [[archaeological excavation|excavated]] by [[Tokyo University]]. [[Grave goods]] recovered include [[Sue pottery]], [[Shinju-kyo|bronze mirrors]], straight iron swords, parts of armor, horse fittings and items of jewellery. From these grave goods, it is estimated that these tumuli were constructed from the late 5th century to the late 6th century.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The two sites flank a large moated late [[Yayoi period]] to early Kofun-period settlement, the [[Hida Sites|Hida Site]], which has a separate National Historic Site designation. The Kannondaira cluster is to the north, and the Tenjindō cluster is to the south, and these areas may have been the necropolis for this settlement. As the area was mostly covered in forest, the state of preservation was relatively good, although even in 1976 it had been reported that a number of the known ''kofun'' has been destroyed due to urban encroachment, road construction, landslides and robbery. After the designation as a National Historic Site, the area has been cleared and opened to the public as an [[archaeological park]], with a small museum to display some of the artifacts found.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

{{Short description|Archaeological site in Myōkō, Hokuriku, Japan}} {{Use American English|date=April 2021}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} | name = Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun group | native_name = 観音平・天神堂古墳群 | native_name_lang = | image =Kan-nondaira Kofun Group, gaikan.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Kofun in the Kannondaira Kofun group | map_type = Japan Niigata Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun group | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|37|03|36|N|138|13|55|E|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Myōkō, Niigata]], [[Japan]] | region = [[Hokuriku region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = 101,160 sq meters | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = | abandoned = | epochs = [[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes | Historic Site = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = | notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} }} The {{nihongo|'''Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster'''|観音平・天神堂古墳群|Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun-gun}} is an [[archaeological site]] containing two separate groups of early to middle[[Kofun period]] [[kofun|burial tumulii]] located in what is now part of the city of [[Myōkō, Niigata]] in the [[Hokuriku region]] of [[Japan]]. The site was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1978.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/201486 |title=観音平・天神堂古墳群|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 30, 2020}}</ref>
==Overview== The Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster consists of two separate groups of ''kofun'', approximately {{Convert|1|km|4=1|sp=us|spell=in}} apart, located approximately 10 minutes by car from [[Arai Station (Niigata)|Arai Station]] on the [[JR East]] [[Shinetsu Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The '''Kannondaira Site''' contains three groups of approximately 53 tumuli, including one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tomb]] ({{nihongo|''zenpō-kōen-fun''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}) dating from the 3rd century. Most of the tombs are {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=dome-shaped|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ({{nihongo|''empun''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), although one is {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=scallop-shaped|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{nihongo|''hotategai-gata kofun''|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}) and some are {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-shaped|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{nihongo|''hōfun''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}), indicating that the site is from a transitional period between the [[Yayoi period]] and the Kofun period. ''[[Haniwa]]'' and ''[[fukiishi]]'' have been recovered from the area. The keyhole-shaped tomb is designated No.4 in the group, and has a total length of {{Convert|33.6|m|sp=us}}, with a dome-portion measuring {{Convert|19.0|by|23.0|m|sp=us}}, and a trapezoidal portion with length of {{Convert|11.6|m|sp=us}} and width of {{Convert|7.0|m|sp=us}}, narrowing to {{Convert|5.0|m|sp=us}} at the "neck" where it connects with the dome. No [[grave goods]] were found in this tomb.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The '''Tenjindō Site''' also consists of three groups of tumuli, of which 188 have thus far been catalogued, making it one of the largest sites in Niigata Prefecture. Almost all of the tumuli are small and dome-shaped, with diameters between {{Convert|5|and|25|m|sp=us|spell=in}}. The site has been repeatedly [[archaeological excavation|excavated]] by [[Tokyo University]]. [[Grave goods]] recovered include [[Sue pottery]], [[Shinju-kyo|bronze mirrors]], straight iron swords, parts of armor, horse fittings and items of jewellery. From these grave goods, it is estimated that these tumuli were constructed from the late 5th century to the late 6th century.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The two sites flank a large moated late [[Yayoi period]] to early Kofun-period settlement, the [[Hida Sites|Hida Site]], which has a separate National Historic Site designation. The Kannondaira cluster is to the north, and the Tenjindō cluster is to the south, and these areas may have been the necropolis for this settlement. As the area was mostly covered in forest, the state of preservation was relatively good, although even in 1976 it had been reported that a number of the known ''kofun'' has been destroyed due to urban encroachment, road construction, landslides and robbery. After the designation as a National Historic Site, the area has been cleared and opened to the public as an [[archaeological park]], with a small museum to display some of the artifacts found.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

Most of the tombs are {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=dome-shaped|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} ({{nihongo|''empun''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), although one is {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=scallop-shaped|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=}} ({{nihongo|''hotategai-gata kofun''|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}) and some are {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-shaped|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} ({{nihongo|''hōfun''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}), indicating that the site is from a transitional period between the [[Yayoi period]] and the Kofun period. ''[[Haniwa]]'' and ''[[fukiishi]]'' have been recovered from the area. The keyhole-shaped tomb is designated No.4 in the group, and has a total length of {{Convert|33.6|m|sp=us}}, with a dome-portion measuring {{Convert|19.0|by|23.0|m|sp=us}}, and a trapezoidal portion with length of {{Convert|11.6|m|sp=us}} and width of {{Convert|7.0|m|sp=us}}, narrowing to {{Convert|5.0|m|sp=us}} at the "neck" where it connects with the dome. No [[grave goods]] were found in this tomb.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The '''Tenjindō Site''' also consists of three groups of tumuli, of which 188 have thus far been catalogued, making it one of the largest sites in Niigata Prefecture. Almost all of the tumuli are small and dome-shaped, with diameters between {{Convert|5|and|25|m|sp=us|spell=in}}. The site has been repeatedly [[archaeological excavation|excavated]] by [[Tokyo University]]. [[Grave goods]] recovered include [[Sue pottery]], [[Shinju-kyo|bronze mirrors]], straight iron swords, parts of armor, horse fittings and items of jewellery. From these grave goods, it is estimated that these tumuli were constructed from the late 5th century to the late 6th century.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The two sites flank a large moated late [[Yayoi period]] to early Kofun-period settlement, the [[Hida Sites|Hida Site]], which has a separate National Historic Site designation. The Kannondaira cluster is to the north, and the Tenjindō cluster is to the south, and these areas may have been the necropolis for this settlement. As the area was mostly covered in forest, the state of preservation was relatively good, although even in 1976 it had been reported that a number of the known ''kofun'' has been destroyed due to urban encroachment, road construction, landslides and robbery. After the designation as a National Historic Site, the area has been cleared and opened to the public as an [[archaeological park]], with a small museum to display some of the artifacts found.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

{{Short description|Archaeological site in Myōkō, Hokuriku, Japan}} {{Use American English|date=April 2021}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=}} | name = Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun group | native_name = 観音平・天神堂古墳群 | native_name_lang = | image =Kan-nondaira Kofun Group, gaikan.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Kofun in the Kannondaira Kofun group | map_type = Japan Niigata Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun group | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|37|03|36|N|138|13|55|E|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Myōkō, Niigata]], [[Japan]] | region = [[Hokuriku region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = 101,160 sq meters | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = | abandoned = | epochs = [[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes | Historic Site = | website = | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = | notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} }} The {{nihongo|'''Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster'''|観音平・天神堂古墳群|Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun-gun}} is an [[archaeological site]] containing two separate groups of early to middle[[Kofun period]] [[kofun|burial tumulii]] located in what is now part of the city of [[Myōkō, Niigata]] in the [[Hokuriku region]] of [[Japan]]. The site was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1978.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/201486 |title=観音平・天神堂古墳群|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 30, 2020}}</ref>
==Overview== The Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster consists of two separate groups of ''kofun'', approximately {{Convert|1|km|4=1|sp=us|spell=in}} apart, located approximately 10 minutes by car from [[Arai Station (Niigata)|Arai Station]] on the [[JR East]] [[Shinetsu Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The '''Kannondaira Site''' contains three groups of approximately 53 tumuli, including one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tomb]] ({{nihongo|''zenpō-kōen-fun''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}) dating from the 3rd century. Most of the tombs are {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=dome-shaped|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} ({{nihongo|''empun''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), although one is {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=scallop-shaped|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=}} ({{nihongo|''hotategai-gata kofun''|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}) and some are {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-shaped|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} ({{nihongo|''hōfun''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}), indicating that the site is from a transitional period between the [[Yayoi period]] and the Kofun period. ''[[Haniwa]]'' and ''[[fukiishi]]'' have been recovered from the area. The keyhole-shaped tomb is designated No.4 in the group, and has a total length of {{Convert|33.6|m|sp=us}}, with a dome-portion measuring {{Convert|19.0|by|23.0|m|sp=us}}, and a trapezoidal portion with length of {{Convert|11.6|m|sp=us}} and width of {{Convert|7.0|m|sp=us}}, narrowing to {{Convert|5.0|m|sp=us}} at the "neck" where it connects with the dome. No [[grave goods]] were found in this tomb.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The '''Tenjindō Site''' also consists of three groups of tumuli, of which 188 have thus far been catalogued, making it one of the largest sites in Niigata Prefecture. Almost all of the tumuli are small and dome-shaped, with diameters between {{Convert|5|and|25|m|sp=us|spell=in}}. The site has been repeatedly [[archaeological excavation|excavated]] by [[Tokyo University]]. [[Grave goods]] recovered include [[Sue pottery]], [[Shinju-kyo|bronze mirrors]], straight iron swords, parts of armor, horse fittings and items of jewellery. From these grave goods, it is estimated that these tumuli were constructed from the late 5th century to the late 6th century.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The two sites flank a large moated late [[Yayoi period]] to early Kofun-period settlement, the [[Hida Sites|Hida Site]], which has a separate National Historic Site designation. The Kannondaira cluster is to the north, and the Tenjindō cluster is to the south, and these areas may have been the necropolis for this settlement. As the area was mostly covered in forest, the state of preservation was relatively good, although even in 1976 it had been reported that a number of the known ''kofun'' has been destroyed due to urban encroachment, road construction, landslides and robbery. After the designation as a National Historic Site, the area has been cleared and opened to the public as an [[archaeological park]], with a small museum to display some of the artifacts found.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

{{Short description|Archaeological site in Myōkō, Hokuriku, Japan}} {{Use American English|date=April 2021}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} | name = Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun group | native_name = 観音平・天神堂古墳群 | native_name_lang = | image =Kan-nondaira Kofun Group, gaikan.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Kofun in the Kannondaira Kofun group | map_type = Japan Niigata Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun group | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|37|03|36|N|138|13|55|E|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Myōkō, Niigata]], [[Japan]] | region = [[Hokuriku region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = 101,160 sq meters | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = | abandoned = | epochs = [[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes | Historic Site = | website = | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = | notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} }} The {{nihongo|'''Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster'''|観音平・天神堂古墳群|Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun-gun}} is an [[archaeological site]] containing two separate groups of early to middle[[Kofun period]] [[kofun|burial tumulii]] located in what is now part of the city of [[Myōkō, Niigata]] in the [[Hokuriku region]] of [[Japan]]. The site was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1978.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/201486 |title=観音平・天神堂古墳群|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 30, 2020}}</ref>
==Overview== The Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster consists of two separate groups of ''kofun'', approximately {{Convert|1|km|4=1|sp=us|spell=in}} apart, located approximately 10 minutes by car from [[Arai Station (Niigata)|Arai Station]] on the [[JR East]] [[Shinetsu Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The '''Kannondaira Site''' contains three groups of approximately 53 tumuli, including one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tomb]] ({{nihongo|''zenpō-kōen-fun''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}) dating from the 3rd century. Most of the tombs are {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=dome-shaped|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''empun''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), although one is {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=scallop-shaped|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''hotategai-gata kofun''|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}) and some are {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-shaped|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''hōfun''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}), indicating that the site is from a transitional period between the [[Yayoi period]] and the Kofun period. ''[[Haniwa]]'' and ''[[fukiishi]]'' have been recovered from the area. The keyhole-shaped tomb is designated No.4 in the group, and has a total length of {{Convert|33.6|m|sp=us}}, with a dome-portion measuring {{Convert|19.0|by|23.0|m|sp=us}}, and a trapezoidal portion with length of {{Convert|11.6|m|sp=us}} and width of {{Convert|7.0|m|sp=us}}, narrowing to {{Convert|5.0|m|sp=us}} at the "neck" where it connects with the dome. No [[grave goods]] were found in this tomb.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The '''Tenjindō Site''' also consists of three groups of tumuli, of which 188 have thus far been catalogued, making it one of the largest sites in Niigata Prefecture. Almost all of the tumuli are small and dome-shaped, with diameters between {{Convert|5|and|25|m|sp=us|spell=in}}. The site has been repeatedly [[archaeological excavation|excavated]] by [[Tokyo University]]. [[Grave goods]] recovered include [[Sue pottery]], [[Shinju-kyo|bronze mirrors]], straight iron swords, parts of armor, horse fittings and items of jewellery. From these grave goods, it is estimated that these tumuli were constructed from the late 5th century to the late 6th century.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The two sites flank a large moated late [[Yayoi period]] to early Kofun-period settlement, the [[Hida Sites|Hida Site]], which has a separate National Historic Site designation. The Kannondaira cluster is to the north, and the Tenjindō cluster is to the south, and these areas may have been the necropolis for this settlement. As the area was mostly covered in forest, the state of preservation was relatively good, although even in 1976 it had been reported that a number of the known ''kofun'' has been destroyed due to urban encroachment, road construction, landslides and robbery. After the designation as a National Historic Site, the area has been cleared and opened to the public as an [[archaeological park]], with a small museum to display some of the artifacts found.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
==See also== *[[List of Historic Sites of Japan (Niigata)]]
==References== {{reflist}}
==External links== *[http://www.city.myoko.niigata.jp/intropark/533.html Myōkō city official home page] {{in lang|ja}}

The '''Kannondaira Site''' contains three groups of approximately 53 tumuli, including one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tomb]] ({{nihongo|''zenpō-kōen-fun''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}) dating from the 3rd century. Most of the tombs are {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=dome-shaped|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''empun''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), although one is {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=scallop-shaped|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''hotategai-gata kofun''|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}) and some are {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-shaped|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''hōfun''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}), indicating that the site is from a transitional period between the [[Yayoi period]] and the Kofun period. ''[[Haniwa]]'' and ''[[fukiishi]]'' have been recovered from the area. The keyhole-shaped tomb is designated No.4 in the group, and has a total length of {{Convert|33.6|m|sp=us}}, with a dome-portion measuring {{Convert|19.0|by|23.0|m|sp=us}}, and a trapezoidal portion with length of {{Convert|11.6|m|sp=us}} and width of {{Convert|7.0|m|sp=us}}, narrowing to {{Convert|5.0|m|sp=us}} at the "neck" where it connects with the dome. No [[grave goods]] were found in this tomb.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The '''Tenjindō Site''' also consists of three groups of tumuli, of which 188 have thus far been catalogued, making it one of the largest sites in Niigata Prefecture. Almost all of the tumuli are small and dome-shaped, with diameters between {{Convert|5|and|25|m|sp=us|spell=in}}. The site has been repeatedly [[archaeological excavation|excavated]] by [[Tokyo University]]. [[Grave goods]] recovered include [[Sue pottery]], [[Shinju-kyo|bronze mirrors]], straight iron swords, parts of armor, horse fittings and items of jewellery. From these grave goods, it is estimated that these tumuli were constructed from the late 5th century to the late 6th century.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

The Kannondaira cluster is to the north, and the Tenjindō cluster is to the south, and these areas may have been the necropolis for this settlement. As the area was mostly covered in forest, the state of preservation was relatively good, although even in 1976 it had been reported that a number of the known ''kofun'' has been destroyed due to urban encroachment, road construction, landslides and robbery. {{Short description|Archaeological site in Myōkō, Hokuriku, Japan}} {{Use American English|date=April 2021}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} | name = Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun group | native_name = 観音平・天神堂古墳群 | native_name_lang = | image =Kan-nondaira Kofun Group, gaikan.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Kofun in the Kannondaira Kofun group | map_type = Japan Niigata Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun group | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|37|03|36|N|138|13|55|E|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Myōkō, Niigata]], [[Japan]] | region = [[:en:Hokuriku region|Hokuriku region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = 101,160 sq meters | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = | abandoned = | epochs = [[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes | Historic Site = | website = | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = | notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} }} The {{nihongo|'''Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster'''|観音平・天神堂古墳群|Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun-gun}} is an [[:en:Archaeological site|Archaeological site]] containing two separate groups of early to middle[[Kofun period]] [[kofun|burial tumulii]] located in what is now part of the city of [[Myōkō, Niigata]] in the [[:en:Hokuriku region|Hokuriku region]] of [[Japan]]. The site was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1978.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/201486 |title=観音平・天神堂古墳群|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 30, 2020}}</ref>
==Overview== The Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster consists of two separate groups of ''kofun'', approximately {{Convert|1|km|4=1|sp=us|spell=in}} apart, located approximately 10 minutes by car from [[:en:Arai Station (Niigata)|Arai Station]] on the [[JR East]] [[Shinetsu Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The '''Kannondaira Site''' contains three groups of approximately 53 tumuli, including one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tomb]] ({{nihongo|''zenpō-kōen-fun''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}) dating from the 3rd century. Most of the tombs are {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=dome-shaped|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''empun''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), although one is {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=scallop-shaped|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''hotategai-gata kofun''|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}) and some are {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-shaped|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''hōfun''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}), indicating that the site is from a transitional period between the [[Yayoi period]] and the Kofun period. ''[[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]]'' and ''[[fukiishi]]'' have been recovered from the area. The keyhole-shaped tomb is designated No.4 in the group, and has a total length of {{Convert|33.6|m|sp=us}}, with a dome-portion measuring {{Convert|19.0|by|23.0|m|sp=us}}, and a trapezoidal portion with length of {{Convert|11.6|m|sp=us}} and width of {{Convert|7.0|m|sp=us}}, narrowing to {{Convert|5.0|m|sp=us}} at the "neck" where it connects with the dome. No [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] were found in this tomb.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The '''Tenjindō Site''' also consists of three groups of tumuli, of which 188 have thus far been catalogued, making it one of the largest sites in Niigata Prefecture. Almost all of the tumuli are small and dome-shaped, with diameters between {{Convert|5|and|25|m|sp=us|spell=in}}. The site has been repeatedly [[archaeological excavation|excavated]] by [[Tokyo University]]. [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] recovered include [[Sue pottery]], [[Shinju-kyo|bronze mirrors]], straight iron swords, parts of armor, horse fittings and items of jewellery. From these grave goods, it is estimated that these tumuli were constructed from the late 5th century to the late 6th century.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The two sites flank a large moated late [[Yayoi period]] to early Kofun-period settlement, the [[:en:Hida Sites|Hida Site]], which has a separate National Historic Site designation. The Kannondaira cluster is to the north, and the Tenjindō cluster is to the south, and these areas may have been the necropolis for this settlement. As the area was mostly covered in forest, the state of preservation was relatively good, although even in 1976 it had been reported that a number of the known ''kofun'' has been destroyed due to urban encroachment, road construction, landslides and robbery. After the designation as a National Historic Site, the area has been cleared and opened to the public as an [[:en:Archaeological park|Archaeological park]], with a small museum to display some of the artifacts found.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
==See also== *[[List of Historic Sites of Japan (Niigata)]]
==References== {{reflist}}
==External links== *[http://www.city.myoko.niigata.jp/intropark/533.html Myōkō city official home page] {{in lang|ja}}

The '''Kannondaira Site''' contains three groups of approximately 53 tumuli, including one [[Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tomb]] ({{nihongo|''zenpō-kōen-fun''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}) dating from the 3rd century. Most of the tombs are {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=dome-shaped|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''empun''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), although one is {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=scallop-shaped|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''hotategai-gata kofun''|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}) and some are {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-shaped|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''hōfun''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}), indicating that the site is from a transitional period between the [[Yayoi period]] and the Kofun period. ''[[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]]'' and ''[[fukiishi]]'' have been recovered from the area. The keyhole-shaped tomb is designated No.4 in the group, and has a total length of {{Convert|33.6|m|sp=us}}, with a dome-portion measuring {{Convert|19.0|by|23.0|m|sp=us}}, and a trapezoidal portion with length of {{Convert|11.6|m|sp=us}} and width of {{Convert|7.0|m|sp=us}}, narrowing to {{Convert|5.0|m|sp=us}} at the "neck" where it connects with the dome. No [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] were found in this tomb.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The '''Tenjindō Site''' also consists of three groups of tumuli, of which 188 have thus far been catalogued, making it one of the largest sites in Niigata Prefecture. Almost all of the tumuli are small and dome-shaped, with diameters between {{Convert|5|and|25|m|sp=us|spell=in}}. The site has been repeatedly [[archaeological excavation|excavated]] by [[Tokyo University]]. [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] recovered include [[Sue pottery]], [[Shinju-kyo|bronze mirrors]], straight iron swords, parts of armor, horse fittings and items of jewellery. From these grave goods, it is estimated that these tumuli were constructed from the late 5th century to the late 6th century.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The two sites flank a large moated late [[Yayoi period]] to early Kofun-period settlement, the [[:en:Hida Sites|Hida Site]], which has a separate National Historic Site designation. The Kannondaira cluster is to the north, and the Tenjindō cluster is to the south, and these areas may have been the necropolis for this settlement. As the area was mostly covered in forest, the state of preservation was relatively good, although even in 1976 it had been reported that a number of the known ''kofun'' has been destroyed due to urban encroachment, road construction, landslides and robbery. After the designation as a National Historic Site, the area has been cleared and opened to the public as an [[:en:Archaeological park|Archaeological park]], with a small museum to display some of the artifacts found.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

Most of the tombs are {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=dome-shaped|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''empun''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), although one is {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=scallop-shaped|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''hotategai-gata kofun''|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}) and some are {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-shaped|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''hōfun''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}), indicating that the site is from a transitional period between the [[:en:Yayoi period|Yayoi period]] and the Kofun period. ''[[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]]'' and ''[[fukiishi]]'' have been recovered from the area. The keyhole-shaped tomb is designated No.4 in the group, and has a total length of {{Convert|33.6|m|sp=us}}, with a dome-portion measuring {{Convert|19.0|by|23.0|m|sp=us}}, and a trapezoidal portion with length of {{Convert|11.6|m|sp=us}} and width of {{Convert|7.0|m|sp=us}}, narrowing to {{Convert|5.0|m|sp=us}} at the "neck" where it connects with the dome. No [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] were found in this tomb.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The '''Tenjindō Site''' also consists of three groups of tumuli, of which 188 have thus far been catalogued, making it one of the largest sites in Niigata Prefecture. Almost all of the tumuli are small and dome-shaped, with diameters between {{Convert|5|and|25|m|sp=us|spell=in}}. The site has been repeatedly [[archaeological excavation|excavated]] by [[Tokyo University]]. [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] recovered include [[Sue pottery]], [[Shinju-kyo|bronze mirrors]], straight iron swords, parts of armor, horse fittings and items of jewellery. From these grave goods, it is estimated that these tumuli were constructed from the late 5th century to the late 6th century.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The two sites flank a large moated late [[:en:Yayoi period|Yayoi period]] to early Kofun-period settlement, the [[:en:Hida Sites|Hida Site]], which has a separate National Historic Site designation. The Kannondaira cluster is to the north, and the Tenjindō cluster is to the south, and these areas may have been the necropolis for this settlement. As the area was mostly covered in forest, the state of preservation was relatively good, although even in 1976 it had been reported that a number of the known ''kofun'' has been destroyed due to urban encroachment, road construction, landslides and robbery. After the designation as a National Historic Site, the area has been cleared and opened to the public as an [[:en:Archaeological park|Archaeological park]], with a small museum to display some of the artifacts found.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

Most of the tombs are {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=dome-shaped|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''empun''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), although one is {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=scallop-shaped|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''hotategai-gata kofun''|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}) and some are {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-shaped|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''hōfun''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}), indicating that the site is from a transitional period between the [[:en:Yayoi period|Yayoi period]] and the Kofun period. ''[[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]]'' and ''[[fukiishi]]'' have been recovered from the area. The keyhole-shaped tomb is designated No.4 in the group, and has a total length of {{Convert|33.6|m|sp=us}}, with a dome-portion measuring {{Convert|19.0|by|23.0|m|sp=us}}, and a trapezoidal portion with length of {{Convert|11.6|m|sp=us}} and width of {{Convert|7.0|m|sp=us}}, narrowing to {{Convert|5.0|m|sp=us}} at the "neck" where it connects with the dome. No [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] were found in this tomb.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The '''Tenjindō Site''' also consists of three groups of tumuli, of which 188 have thus far been catalogued, making it one of the largest sites in Niigata Prefecture. Almost all of the tumuli are small and dome-shaped, with diameters between {{Convert|5|and|25|m|sp=us|spell=in}}. The site has been repeatedly [[archaeological excavation|excavated]] by [[:en:Tokyo University|Tokyo University]]. [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] recovered include [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]], [[Shinju-kyo|bronze mirrors]], straight iron swords, parts of armor, horse fittings and items of jewellery. From these grave goods, it is estimated that these tumuli were constructed from the late 5th century to the late 6th century.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The two sites flank a large moated late [[:en:Yayoi period|Yayoi period]] to early Kofun-period settlement, the [[:en:Hida Sites|Hida Site]], which has a separate National Historic Site designation. The Kannondaira cluster is to the north, and the Tenjindō cluster is to the south, and these areas may have been the necropolis for this settlement. As the area was mostly covered in forest, the state of preservation was relatively good, although even in 1976 it had been reported that a number of the known ''kofun'' has been destroyed due to urban encroachment, road construction, landslides and robbery. After the designation as a National Historic Site, the area has been cleared and opened to the public as an [[:en:Archaeological park|Archaeological park]], with a small museum to display some of the artifacts found.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

The '''Kannondaira Site''' contains three groups of approximately 53 tumuli, including one [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tomb]] ({{nihongo|''zenpō-kōen-fun''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}) dating from the 3rd century. Most of the tombs are {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=dome-shaped|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''empun''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), although one is {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=scallop-shaped|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''hotategai-gata kofun''|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}) and some are {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-shaped|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''hōfun''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}), indicating that the site is from a transitional period between the [[:en:Yayoi period|Yayoi period]] and the Kofun period. ''[[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]]'' and ''[[fukiishi]]'' have been recovered from the area. The keyhole-shaped tomb is designated No.4 in the group, and has a total length of {{Convert|33.6|m|sp=us}}, with a dome-portion measuring {{Convert|19.0|by|23.0|m|sp=us}}, and a trapezoidal portion with length of {{Convert|11.6|m|sp=us}} and width of {{Convert|7.0|m|sp=us}}, narrowing to {{Convert|5.0|m|sp=us}} at the "neck" where it connects with the dome. No [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] were found in this tomb.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The '''Tenjindō Site''' also consists of three groups of tumuli, of which 188 have thus far been catalogued, making it one of the largest sites in Niigata Prefecture. Almost all of the tumuli are small and dome-shaped, with diameters between {{Convert|5|and|25|m|sp=us|spell=in}}. The site has been repeatedly [[archaeological excavation|excavated]] by [[:en:Tokyo University|Tokyo University]]. [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] recovered include [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]], [[Shinju-kyo|bronze mirrors]], straight iron swords, parts of armor, horse fittings and items of jewellery. From these grave goods, it is estimated that these tumuli were constructed from the late 5th century to the late 6th century.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The two sites flank a large moated late [[:en:Yayoi period|Yayoi period]] to early Kofun-period settlement, the [[:en:Hida Sites|Hida Site]], which has a separate National Historic Site designation. The Kannondaira cluster is to the north, and the Tenjindō cluster is to the south, and these areas may have been the necropolis for this settlement. As the area was mostly covered in forest, the state of preservation was relatively good, although even in 1976 it had been reported that a number of the known ''kofun'' has been destroyed due to urban encroachment, road construction, landslides and robbery. After the designation as a National Historic Site, the area has been cleared and opened to the public as an [[:en:Archaeological park|Archaeological park]], with a small museum to display some of the artifacts found.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

The site was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1978.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/201486 |title=観音平・天神堂古墳群|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 30, 2020}}</ref>
==Overview== The Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun cluster consists of two separate groups of ''kofun'', approximately {{Convert|1|km|4=1|sp=us|spell=in}} apart, located approximately 10 minutes by car from [[:en:Arai Station (Niigata)|Arai Station]] on the [[:en:East Japan Railway Company|East Japan Railway Company]] [[:en:Shinetsu Main Line|Shinetsu Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The '''Kannondaira Site''' contains three groups of approximately 53 tumuli, including one [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|keyhole-shaped tomb]] ({{nihongo|''zenpō-kōen-fun''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=[[Zenpokoenfun]]|2=前方後円墳|3=|4=}}) dating from the 3rd century. Most of the tombs are {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=dome-shaped|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''empun''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), although one is {{ill|scallop-shaped kofun|lt=scallop-shaped|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''hotategai-gata kofun''|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun}}) and some are {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-shaped|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ({{nihongo|''hōfun''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}), indicating that the site is from a transitional period between the [[:en:Yayoi period|Yayoi period]] and the Kofun period. ''[[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]]'' and ''[[fukiishi]]'' have been recovered from the area. The keyhole-shaped tomb is designated No.4 in the group, and has a total length of {{Convert|33.6|m|sp=us}}, with a dome-portion measuring {{Convert|19.0|by|23.0|m|sp=us}}, and a trapezoidal portion with length of {{Convert|11.6|m|sp=us}} and width of {{Convert|7.0|m|sp=us}}, narrowing to {{Convert|5.0|m|sp=us}} at the "neck" where it connects with the dome. No [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] were found in this tomb.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The '''Tenjindō Site''' also consists of three groups of tumuli, of which 188 have thus far been catalogued, making it one of the largest sites in Niigata Prefecture. Almost all of the tumuli are small and dome-shaped, with diameters between {{Convert|5|and|25|m|sp=us|spell=in}}. The site has been repeatedly [[archaeological excavation|excavated]] by [[:en:Tokyo University|Tokyo University]]. [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] recovered include [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]], [[Shinju-kyo|bronze mirrors]], straight iron swords, parts of armor, horse fittings and items of jewellery. From these grave goods, it is estimated that these tumuli were constructed from the late 5th century to the late 6th century.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The two sites flank a large moated late [[:en:Yayoi period|Yayoi period]] to early Kofun-period settlement, the [[:en:Hida Sites|Hida Site]], which has a separate National Historic Site designation. The Kannondaira cluster is to the north, and the Tenjindō cluster is to the south, and these areas may have been the necropolis for this settlement. As the area was mostly covered in forest, the state of preservation was relatively good, although even in 1976 it had been reported that a number of the known ''kofun'' has been destroyed due to urban encroachment, road construction, landslides and robbery. After the designation as a National Historic Site, the area has been cleared and opened to the public as an [[:en:Archaeological park|Archaeological park]], with a small museum to display some of the artifacts found.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
